## Function  
  
I created a function to process a single year of data; this included improved formatting of column names and variable types, removing duplicate data, averaging over multiple measures on the same day, returning one row per date per year, and exporting a tibble with the cleaned data. Because I shortened the column names for the cleaned data, I decided to add a data dictionary to the project so as to not lose any information about the data.

```{r}
## Purpose: clean air quality measurements for a single year of data
## Arguments: 
##    file_path, character, path to where .csv dataset is located on computer
##    ozone_units, character, specifies either "ppm" or "ppb", default is "ppm"
## Returns:
##    data_year, tibble, cleaned data set for one year

csv_clean <- function(file_path, ozone_units = "ppm") {

  ## Check requirements for function
  if(!is.character(file_path)) {
    stop("Error: file_path is not a character string!")
  }
  
  
  if(!ozone_units %in% c("ppm", "ppb")) {
    stop("Error: ozone_units must be either 'ppm' or 'ppb'")
  }
  
  if(!is.character(ozone_units)) {
    stop("Error: ozone_units is not a character string!")
  }
  
  ## Load data
  data_year <- read_csv(file_path)
  
  ## Rename pollutant concentration columns
  data_year <- data_year |> 
    rename(
      date = Date,
      CO = `Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration`,
      PM25 = `Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration`,
      O3 = `Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration`
    )
  
  ## Format date 
  data_year <- data_year |> 
    mutate(
      date = as.Date(date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
    )
  
  ## Remove duplicate rows
  data_year <- data_year |> 
    distinct()
  
  ## Set negative pollutant concentrations to zero
  for (i in c("CO","PM25", "O3")) {
    data_year[[i]][data_year[[i]] < 0] <- 0
  }
  
  ## Calculate daily averages for repeated dates
  data_year <- data_year |> 
    group_by(date) |> 
    summarise(
      CO = mean(CO, na.rm = TRUE),
      PM25 = mean(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
      O3 = mean(O3, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  ## Add back the units columns for CO and PM2.5
  data_year <- data_year |> 
    mutate(
      units_CO = "ppm",
      units_PM = "ug/m3 LC"
    )
  
  ## Convert ozone units if needed:
  ## Convert ppm --> ppb numerically
  if (ozone_units == "ppb") {
    data_year$O3 <- data_year$O3 * 1000
  }
  
  ## Change the ozone units column
  data_year <- data_year |> 
    mutate(units_O3 = ozone_units)
  
  ## Reorder columns
  data_year <- data_year |> 
    select(
      date,
      CO,
      units_CO,
      PM25,
      units_PM, 
      O3,
      units_O3
    )
  
  ## Return cleaned data as a tibble
  return(data_year)
}
```

```{r include=FALSE}
## Running the function to clean each year of data, returns a tibble
clean_2018 <- csv_clean("AQ_2018.csv", "ppm")
clean_2019 <- csv_clean("AQ_2019.csv", "ppm")
clean_2020 <- csv_clean("AQ_2020.csv", "ppm")
```

## Tables  
  
I created a function to make a table for each year of data (2018, 2019, and 2020) that shows the minimum and maximum daily concentrations of each pollutant. This function takes the fully cleaned data set (cleaned data for all years combined into one tibble) and the year (2018, 2019, or 2020) as arguments, separates the data by the desired year, and then generates a table that contains the name and units of each pollutant, displays the numeric values to 3 decimal places, and includes a title/caption. 
  
```{r}
## Pseudo code: 
## Title: {year} min and max
## cols: Min | Max 
## Rows: CO (ppm), PM25 (ug/m3 LC), O3 (ppm OR ppb)
## Takes in clean_data
## Filters by year using filter() 
## uses summarise() function to create max and min, round decimal place to 3 values
## Saves to a data frame/tibble
## if ozone_units == "ppm" --> O3 (ppm) row name
## if ozone_units == "ppb" --> O3 (ppb) row name
## returns table using gt() function


## Table Function:
## Purpose: create a table of the minimum and maximum daily concentrations of
## each pollutant using processed data for all years
## Arguments:
##    clean_data, tibble, cleaned data for all years with one row per date
##    year, numeric, year represented by data set
## Returns:
##    summary_table, gt_tbl/list, shows min and max daily concentrations of CO, 
##    PM2.5, and O3 with measurement units, rounded to 3 decimal places


create_table <- function(clean_data, year) {
  
  ## Checking argument requirements
  if(!year %in% c(2018, 2019, 2020)) {
    stop("Error: year must be 2018, 2019, or 2020!")
  }
  
  if(!is.numeric(year)) {
    stop("Error: year is not numeric!")
  }
  
  if(!is_tibble(clean_data) | !is.data.frame(clean_data)) {
    stop("Error: clean_data is not a tibble or data frame!")
  }
  
  
  ## Filter data set by year
  data_year <- clean_data |> filter(lubridate::year(date) == year)
  
  ## Calculate min and max concentrations for each of the three pollutants
  ## Because NA's are present in the pollutant columns, we set na.rm = TRUE
  summary_table <- data_year |> 
    summarise(
      CO_min = min(CO, na.rm = TRUE),
      CO_max = max(CO, na.rm = TRUE),
      PM25_min = min(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
      PM25_max = max(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
      O3_min = min(O3, na.rm = TRUE),
      O3_max = max(O3, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  
  ## Pollutants become the rows, min/max become the columns
  summary_table <- summary_table |> 
    pivot_longer(
      cols = everything(),
      names_to = c("Pollutant", ".value"),
      names_pattern = "(.*)_(min|max)"
    )
  
  ## Add pollutant names and measurement units
  summary_table <- summary_table |> 
    mutate(
      Pollutant = recode(
        Pollutant,
        "CO" = "CO (ppm)",
        "PM25" = "PM2.5 (ug/m3 LC)",
        "O3" = paste0("O3 (", first(clean_data$units_O3), ")")
      ))
  
  ## Format summary table
  summary_table <- summary_table |> 
    gt() |> 
    tab_header(
      title = paste(
        year,
        "Minimum and Maximum Daily Air Pollutant Concentrations"
      )
    ) |> 
    cols_label(
      Pollutant = "Pollutant",
      min = "Minimum",
      max = "Maximum"
    ) |> 
    fmt_number(
      columns = c(min, max),
      decimals = 3
    )
  
  return(summary_table)
}
```
  
Here is the table containing the minimum and maximum daily concentrations of each pollutant for the year 2018: 
```{r}
## Table for 2018
table_2018 <- create_table(clean_data, 2018)
table_2018
```
  
Here is the table containing the minimum and maximum daily concentrations of each pollutant for the year 2019: 
```{r}
## Table for 2019

table_2019
```
  
Here is the table containing the minimum and maximum daily concentrations of each pollutant for the year 2020: 
```{r}
## Table for 2020
table_2020 <- create_table(clean_data, 2020)
table_2020
```
  
## Plots  
  
Note: Because the 2020 data stop in April, January through April are based on three years of data, while May through December are based on two years. 
  
```{r include=FALSE}
## Plot 1: CO and O3 by month 
## X-axis: month
## Y-axis: CO and O3 concentrations, monthly averages (over the 3 years)
## Points with a 95% confidence interval error bars, coded by color 

## Pseudo code:
## For i in 1:12
## If Month == i, calculate n, s, and xbar
## Calculate xbar +/- 1.96 * s/sqrt(n)
## save xbar, upper bound, and lower bounds of confidence interval
## Save in a data frame/tibble

## Plot CO in blue, and O3 in red
clean_data <- clean_data |> 
  ## Add month column, coded 1:12, from the lubridate function
  mutate(month = month(date))

month_summary <- clean_data |> 
  ## Group by months across all relevant years
  group_by(month) |> 
  summarise(
    ## Because NA's are present in clean_data, we set na.rm = TRUE and sum all non-NA values to calculate n
    ## CO statistics
    CO_mean = mean(CO, na.rm = TRUE),
    CO_sd = sd(CO, na.rm = TRUE),
    CO_n = sum(!is.na(CO)),
    
    ## O3 statistics
    O3_mean = mean(O3, na.rm = TRUE),
    O3_sd = sd(O3, na.rm = TRUE),
    O3_n = sum(!is.na(O3)),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## Calculating 95% Confidence Intervals
month_summary <- month_summary |> 
  mutate(
    ## CO onfidence intervals
    CO_lower = CO_mean - 1.96 * (CO_sd / sqrt(CO_n)),
    CO_upper = CO_mean + 1.96 * (CO_sd / sqrt(CO_n)),
    
    ## O3 confidence intervals
    O3_lower = O3_mean - 1.96 * (O3_sd / sqrt(O3_n)),
    O3_upper = O3_mean + 1.96 * (O3_sd / sqrt(O3_n))
  )

## Creating the data to plot
month_plot_data <- month_summary |> 
  pivot_longer(
    ## Arrange columns by month
    cols = -month,
    names_to = c("pollutant", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(CO|O3)_(mean|sd|n|lower|upper)"
  )

## Making month a factor
month_plot_data <- month_plot_data |> 
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month, 
      levels = 1:12,
      labels = month.abb
    )
  )

## Preliminary investigation plot
## From this, multiplying O3 by 10 would help scale the two data
ggplot(
  month_plot_data,
  aes(x = month, 
      y = mean,
      color = pollutant)
) + 
  geom_point(size = 2) + 
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower,
        ymax = upper),
    width = 0.2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~pollutant, scales = "free_y") + 
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "CO" = "blue",
      "O3" = "red"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Average CO and O3 Concentrations (2018-2020)",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean Daily Concentration",
    color = "Pollutant"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal()
```
  
### $CO$ and $O_{3}$ by Month
```{r}
## Plot 1
## Scaling the O3 (ppm) data by 10 
month_plot_data <- month_plot_data |> 
  mutate(
    mean_scaled = ifelse(
      pollutant == "O3", mean * 10, mean),
    lower_scaled = ifelse(
      pollutant == "O3", lower * 10, lower),
    upper_scaled = ifelse(
      pollutant == "O3", upper * 10, upper))

## Plotting
ggplot(month_plot_data,
       aes(
         x = month, 
         y = mean_scaled,
         color = pollutant
       )) + 
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = lower_scaled,
      ymax = upper_scaled
    ),
    linewidth = 0.4,
    width = 0.25
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "CO" = "#1E88E5",
      "O3" = "#D81B60"
    )
  ) + 
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Average CO and O3 Concentrations (2018-2020)",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Concentration (ppm; O3 multiplied by 10)",
    color = "Pollutant",
    caption = "O3 (ppm) concentrations and their confidence intervals were multiplied by 10 to make both seasonal trends visible on the same y-axis. Plotted using color-blind friendly palette."
  ) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
  
For this plot, I chose to multiply the monthly mean $O_{3}$ concentration by 10; multiplying by less than 10 resulted in the error bars of the monthly mean $O_{3}$ concentration being too small to read, and multiply by more than 10 resulted in the monthly mean $O_{3}$ concentration appearing greater overall than the monthly mean $CO$ concentration. Although the error bars overlap for the months of February and October, the monthly mean concentrations for both pollutants remain readable on the same graph and preserve their original patterns.  
  
### $PM_{2.5}$ by Month and Year
```{r}
## Plot 2
## X-axis: month
## Y-axis: PM_2.5 concentration
## color: year

## One PM25 concentration for each month of each year
month_PM25 <- clean_data |> 
  mutate(
    month = month(date),
    year = year(date)
  ) |> 
  group_by(year, month) |> 
  summarise(
    PM25_mean = mean(PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

## Creating month labels
month_PM25 <- month_PM25 |> 
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = 1:12,
      labels = month.abb
    )
  )

## Plotting
ggplot(month_PM25,
       aes(
         x = month,
         y = PM25_mean,
         color = factor(year),
         group = year
       )) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "2018" = "#D81B60",
      "2019" = "#1E88E5",
      "2020" = "#FFC107"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Average PM2.5 Concentrations by Year",
    x = "Month",
    y = expression("Mean PM"[2.5]*" Concentration ("*mu*"g/m"^3*")"),
    color = "Year",
    caption = "Monthly averages are calculated separately for each year. Plotted using color-blind friendly palette."
  ) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
